title: GST Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: GST Calculator: Add or remove GST, with CGST/SGST split. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [GST Calculator](/gst-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Add or remove GST, with CGST/SGST split. Enter your amount, GST rate and action and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Goods and Services Tax is charged on most goods and services. Within a state it splits equally into CGST and SGST; across states it's charged as IGST. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator).

## How to use the GST Calculator

Start by entering your amount, then choosing your GST rate from the list and finally choosing your action from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your amount.
2. Choose your gst rate from the list.
3. Choose your action from the list.
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

GST = Net × rate. Inclusive: Net = Total ÷ (1 + rate).

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [GST Calculator](/gst-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 18% GST on 1,000 is 180 (CGST 90 + SGST 90), for a total of 1,180. Try the same figures in the [GST Calculator](/gst-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Amount: 1000, GST rate: 18%, Action: Add GST (exclusive)), the [GST Calculator](/gst-calculator) returns Total (incl. GST): 1,180, GST amount: 180, CGST / SGST each: 90, Net amount: 1,000. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Check the HSN/SAC code for the correct slab.
- Businesses can claim input tax credit on GST paid.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What are the GST slabs?

The common slabs are 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%, with some essentials at 0%. Try it with your own numbers in the [GST Calculator](/gst-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is IGST?

Integrated GST applies to inter-state sales and equals CGST + SGST combined. Try it with your own numbers in the [GST Calculator](/gst-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the GST Calculator use?

GST = Net × rate. Inclusive: Net = Total ÷ (1 + rate). You can see it in action in the [GST Calculator](/gst-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the GST Calculator?

Just Amount, GST rate and Action. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
